statements.text: The task model carries a nullable `deletedAt` timestamp, serialized in JSON as `deletedAt`: an ISO-8601 string when the task is soft-deleted, and `null` when the task is active.
`DELETE /tasks/{id}` on an existing active task soft-deletes it — it sets `deletedAt` to the current time and returns `204 No Content`.

`DELETE /tasks/{id}` does not permanently remove the task: after a successful delete the task is still retained in the store and is reachable via `GET /tasks?includeDeleted=true` with a non-null `deletedAt`.
`DELETE /tasks/{id}` for an id that does not identify a known task returns `404 Not Found`.
`GET /tasks` returns only active (not soft-deleted) tasks by default.
`GET /tasks?includeDeleted=true` returns all tasks, including soft-deleted ones (whose `deletedAt` is non-null).
`GET /tasks/{id}` returns `404 Not Found` for a soft-deleted task.
The four tasks seeded at startup remain active after startup — each serializes `deletedAt` as `null` — so existing rows keep working without a migration step.
`dotnet build` and `dotnet test` stay green, and the five pre-existing integration tests still pass (R-003).
No unrelated behaviour of the other CRUD endpoints changes: `POST /tasks`, `PUT /tasks/{id}` and the blank-title `400` validation keep their existing contracts.
The boundary direction and naming rules hold: `Domain/**` references no ASP.NET type (R-004) and the work-item enum stays named `TaskState` (R-005).
`DELETE /tasks/{id}` for a task that is already soft-deleted returns `404 Not Found` and leaves the original `deletedAt` unchanged.
`PUT /tasks/{id}` returns `404 Not Found` for a soft-deleted task and does not modify it; its behaviour toward active tasks is unchanged.
